questions.question: Q1(a). Express 2 + 2i in polar form.
questions.solution: r = √(4+4) = 2√2; tanθ = 1 with x,y > 0, θ = 45°. Boxed 2√2(cos45°+i sin45°) (matches the printed key, book p346).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q1(a); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q1(b). Express √3 + i in polar form.
questions.solution: r = √(3+1) = 2; tanθ = 1/√3, first quadrant, θ = 30°. Boxed 2(cos30°+i sin30°) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q1(b); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: 2i lies on the positive imaginary axis: r = 2, θ = 90°.
questions.question: Q1(c). Express 2i in polar form.
questions.solution: r = 2, argument 90°. Boxed 2(cos90°+i sin90°) (matches the printed key; the scan renders the question as '2' but the key's 2(cos90°+i sin90°) = 2i fixes the reading).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q1(c); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: i-√3: x < 0, y > 0 → second quadrant, θ = 150°.
questions.question: Q1(d). Express i - √3 in polar form.
questions.solution: r = √(1+3) = 2; tanθ = -1/√3 with second-quadrant position, θ = 150°. Boxed 2(cos150°+i sin150°) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q1(d); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q1(e). Express 1 - i in polar form.
questions.solution: r = √2; tanθ = -1, fourth quadrant, θ = 315°. Boxed √2(cos315°+i sin315°) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q1(e); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q1(f). Express (1 + i)/(1 - i) in polar form.
questions.solution: (1+i)/(1-i) = (1+i)²/2 = i. r = 1, θ = 90°. Boxed 1·(cos90°+i sin90°) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q1(f); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q1(g). Express i/(1 + i) in polar form.
questions.solution: i(1-i)/2 = (1+i)/2. r = √(1/4+1/4) = 1/√2; tanθ = 1, first quadrant, θ = 45°. Boxed (1/√2)(cos45°+i sin45°) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q1(g); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q1(h). Express √((1 - i)/(1 + i)) in polar form.
questions.solution: (1-i)/(1+i) = (1-i)²/2 = -i. √(-i) = (1-i)/√2 (first-quadrant Convention: x²-y² = 0, 2xy = -1 → (1-i)/√2). r = 1, θ = 315°. Boxed 1·(cos315°+i sin315°) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q1(h); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2(a). Express 3(cos60° + i sin60°) in x + iy form.
questions.solution: 3(1/2)+i·3(√3/2) = 3/2+i3√3/2. Boxed 3/2+i3√3/2 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q2(a); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2(b). Express 3(cos120° + i sin120°) in x + iy form.
questions.solution: 3(-1/2)+i·3(√3/2) = -3/2+i3√3/2. Boxed -3/2+i3√3/2 (matches the printed key).

questions.question: Q2(c). Express 2(cos150° + i sin150°) in x + iy form.
questions.solution: 2(-√3/2)+i·2(1/2) = -√3+i. Boxed -√3+i (matches the printed key).

questions.question: Q2(d). Express 2(cos(-45°) + i sin(-45°)) in x + iy form.
questions.solution: 2(1/√2)+i·2(-1/√2) = √2-i√2. Boxed √2-i√2 (matches the printed key; the key confirms the 2 covers the sine term too).

questions.question: Q3(a). Simplify: (cos32° + i sin32°)(cos13° + i sin13°).

questions.knowledgeNote: sin40°+i cos40° = cos50°+i sin50° first; then 50°+40° = 90°.
questions.question: Q3(b). Simplify: (sin40° + i cos40°)(cos40° + i sin40°).
questions.solution: First factor = cos(90°-40°)+i sin(90°-40°) = cos50°+i sin50°. Product: cos90°+i sin90° = i. Boxed i (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q3(b); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q3(c). Simplify: (cos80° + i sin80°)/(cos20° + i sin20°).
questions.solution: cos60°+i sin60° = 1/2+i√3/2. Boxed 1/2+i√3/2 (matches the printed key).

questions.knowledgeNote: Numerator: 3θ-θ = 2θ; denominator: (cosθ+i sinθ)² = cos2θ+i sin2θ; quotient 1.
questions.question: Q3(d). Simplify: (cos3θ + i sin3θ)(cosθ - i sinθ)/(cosθ + i sinθ)^2.
questions.solution: Numerator = cos(3θ-θ)+i sin(3θ-θ) = cos2θ+i sin2θ. Denominator = cos2θ+i sin2θ. Quotient = 1. Boxed 1 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q3(d); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q5(a). Find the square roots of 4 + 4√3 i (De Moivre or algebraic).
questions.solution: x²-y² = 4, 2xy = 4√3, x²+y² = 8 → 2x² = 12, x = ±√6, y = ±√2 (same sign). Check (√6+i√2)² = 6+2i√12-2 = 4+4√3i ✓. Boxed ±(√6+i√2) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q5(a); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q5(b). Find the square roots of -1 + √3 i.
questions.solution: x²-y² = -1, 2xy = √3, x²+y² = 2 → 2x² = 1, x = ±1/√2; y = ±√3/√2 (opposite signs since xy > 0... 2xy = √3 > 0, same sign). Check ((1+i√3)/√2)² = (1+2i√3-3)/2 = -1+i√3 ✓. Boxed ±(1+i√3)/√2 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q5(b); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q5(c). Find the square roots of -2 - 2√3 i.
questions.solution: x²-y² = -2, 2xy = -2√3, x²+y² = 4 → 2x² = 2, x = ±1, y = ∓√3. Check (-1+i√3)² = 1-2i√3-3 = -2-2i√3 ✓. Boxed ±(-1+i√3) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q5(c); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q5(d). Find the square roots of 2i.
questions.solution: x²-y² = 0, 2xy = 2, x²+y² = 2 → x = ±1, y = ±1 (same sign). Check (1+i)² = 2i ✓. Boxed ±(1+i) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q5(d); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q5(e). Find the square roots of -i.
questions.solution: x²-y² = 0, 2xy = -1, x²+y² = 1 → x = ±1/√2, y = ∓1/√2. Check ((1-i)/√2)² = (1-2i-1)/2 = -i ✓. Boxed ±(1-i)/√2 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q5(e); book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q6. Determine the cube roots of -1.
questions.solution: Angles 60°, 180°, 300°: (1±i√3)/2 and -1. Check: ((1+i√3)/2)³ = ? (cos60°+i sin60°)³ = cos180°+i sin180° = -1 ✓. Boxed -1, (1±i√3)/2 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q6; book p345 = PDF p372 (vision read)

questions.question: Q7(a). Solve z^4 = 1.
questions.solution: z = cos(k·90°)+i sin(k·90°), k = 0,1,2,3: 1, i, -1, -i. Boxed ±1, ±i (matches the printed key).

questions.question: Q7(b). Solve z^6 = 1.

questions.question: Q7(c). Solve z^4 + 1 = 0.
questions.solution: Angles (180°+k·360°)/4 = 45°+k·90°: ±(1+i)/√2, ±(1-i)/√2. Check ((1+i)/√2)⁴ = ((2i)/2)² = i² = -1 ✓. Boxed as shown (matches the printed key).

questions.knowledgeNote: z̄ = r(cosθ-i sinθ); Arg runs clockwise: 2π-θ.
questions.question: Q9. If z̄ is the conjugate of z, prove that Arg(z̄) = 2π - Arg(z).
questions.solution: z = r(cosθ+i sinθ) with θ = Arg(z). z̄ = r(cosθ-i sinθ) = r(cos(2π-θ)+i sin(2π-θ)). So Arg(z̄) = 2π-θ = 2π-Arg(z). ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q9; book p346 = PDF p373 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: zⁿ = cos nθ+i sin nθ; 1/zⁿ = cos nθ-i sin nθ; subtract: 2i sin nθ.
questions.question: Q10. If z = cosθ + i sinθ, prove that z^n - 1/z^n = 2i sin(nθ).
questions.solution: zⁿ = cos nθ+i sin nθ (De Moivre). 1/zⁿ = z̄ⁿ = cos nθ-i sin nθ (since |z| = 1). Subtracting: 2i sin nθ. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.11 Ex 11.4 Q10; book p346 = PDF p373 (vision read)
